h1: The 8 Best Craftsman Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Craftsman Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 leaf blowers from Craftsman V20 to DEWALT and Husqvarna, compared on airflow, speed settings, weight and kit contents.
summary: The Craftsman V20 RP is the best Craftsman leaf blower, with a brushless motor, 410 CFM and a battery and charger in the box. The DEWALT DCBL772B tops the group at 600 CFM but ships as a bare tool. The V20 axial kit at 380 CFM and the 200 CFM blowers suit smaller yards.
intro: Craftsman sells a family of V20 battery blowers that look nearly identical on a shelf and perform quite differently. The difference is in airflow, whether the kit includes a battery and whether the motor is brushless, none of which is obvious from a product photo. A bare tool and a ready kit can share a name and differ by the price of a battery.

We reviewed eight blowers, six of them Craftsman, plus two outside picks from DEWALT and Husqvarna for context. Each was ranked on airflow, speed controls, weight claims and kit contents. We note when the listing is silent on a spec, and we do not fill gaps with guesses. Airflow among the Craftsman models runs from 200 to 410 CFM.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN Leaf Blower Cordless with Battery and Charger V20 RP
products.verdict: 410 CFM, a brushless motor and a battery and charger in the box. The sensible default.
products.description:
The V20 RP lists 410 CFM, a brushless motor and a battery and charger in the box, in the $100 to $200 tier. A brushless motor wastes less energy as heat and has no brushes to wear, so the same battery gives more force and longer runtime. The brand claims 50 percent less noise and 39 percent less weight than gas blowers.

It wins because it is the strongest Craftsman here and arrives ready to use. Against the V20 axial kit it moves 30 CFM more, and against the 200 CFM models it is more than twice as strong. The DEWALT DCBL772B has far more airflow but needs a separate battery, which makes the real cost much higher.

Buy it for a typical suburban yard. The caveat is that the noise and weight figures are the brand's own claims.
pros: Battery and charger in the box
Less noise than gas per the brand
cons: Noise and weight claims are the brand's
Costs more than the cheaper V20 models
products.idealFor: Suburban yards with ordinary leaf fall.

products.name: Dewalt Blower AXIAL HNDHLD 60V 600CFM DCBL772B
products.verdict: 600 CFM from a 60V handheld, the strongest battery blower here. Bare tool.
products.description:
The DEWALT DCBL772B is a 60V axial handheld that lists 600 CFM, sold as a bare tool. An axial design pushes air straight through a high-flow fan, which is why DEWALT can reach 600 CFM in a handheld body. It is the strongest battery tool in this guide by a wide margin.

It ranks second because you must supply a 60V battery, the expensive part of the system. Against the Craftsman V20 RP it moves 190 more CFM, but the RP includes a battery and charger in its price. For anyone who already owns DEWALT 60V packs, the DCBL772B is the stronger pick on pure airflow.

Buy it if you own 60V batteries and fight thick, wet leaves. The caveat is cost, which climbs quickly once you add a pack and charger.
pros: 600 CFM, highest here among battery tools
products.skipIf: You are starting from scratch on a budget.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Axial Leaf Blower Kit
products.verdict: 380 CFM with a dual-speed trigger and an integrated scraper. Light and compact.
products.description:
The V20 axial kit lists 380 CFM, a two-stage trigger, an integrated scraper and a lightweight, compact body, in the $50 to $100 tier. The two-stage trigger lets you ease off near flower beds and open up across open ground, and the scraper loosens stuck debris from a driveway or deck.

It ranks third because it moves 30 CFM less than the V20 RP, but it costs less, a full tier lower. That makes it the best value for a yard of moderate size. The listing gives fewer details on the motor type, so you cannot confirm brushless, unlike the RP, which names it.

A good fit for small to mid-size yards. The caveat is the missing motor information, and for a bigger lawn, the RP is the better tool.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Leaf Blower (3-Speed)
products.verdict: A 3-speed selector with a lock-on trigger and three attachments included.
products.description:
This V20 has a three-speed selector, a lock-on trigger, three included attachments and a compact design for one-handed use, in the $50 to $100 tier. A lock-on trigger holds the throttle so your finger does not tire on a long clean-up, and attachments extend the use to corners and gutters.

It ranks fourth because the listing shows no CFM figure, so you cannot compare it with the others. It costs less than the RP and gives more attachments than any other Craftsman here. Three speeds give finer control than the axial kit's two stages. Battery details are thin, so confirm what is in the box.

A good all-rounder for small jobs. The caveat is the missing airflow number: ask for the CFM before buying.
products.skipIf: You want a stated airflow figure.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 20V MAX Cordless Leaf Blower with Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 200 CFM starter kit with a battery and charger and a nozzle scraper.
products.description:
The 20V MAX lists 200 CFM, includes a battery and charger, and has an integrated nozzle scraper for stubborn debris, in the $100 to $200 tier. It is designed to maneuver in tight spaces, which suits patios and garage floors. Being a complete kit, it works out of the box.

It ranks fifth because 200 CFM is about half of the RP's 410. It does come as a ready kit, which the cheaper V20 listing is not guaranteed to be. It also sits in the same $100 to $200 tier as the RP, which makes the weaker airflow harder to justify unless you want its size. The scraper is a useful extra.

A fit for patios and small yards. The caveat is the airflow: it struggles with wet leaves and large drifts.
products.skipIf: You have a lawn full of leaves.

products.name: CRAFTSMAN V20 Cordless Leaf Blower (200 CFM)
products.verdict: The least expensive pick here, with 200 CFM, a scraper and a wall-storage hook.
products.description:
This V20 lists 200 CFM, an integrated scraper and an integrated hook for VERSATRACK wall storage, at the lowest price in the roundup, in the $50 to $100 tier. The wall hook keeps it off the floor and out of the way in a garage, which many blowers lack.

It ranks sixth because it has the same 200 CFM as the 20V MAX kit but may not include a battery. It is the cheapest way into the Craftsman line, but the cost of a battery and charger can erase the saving. If you own V20 batteries, the equation changes completely.

Buy it if you already own V20 batteries. The caveat is the box contents, so check the listing before ordering.
products.skipIf: You need a battery in the box.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Blower
products.verdict: A DEWALT 20V MAX with a trigger lock-on and three nozzles. Only 100 CFM.
products.description:
The DEWALT 20V MAX blower lists 100 CFM, a trigger lock-on that reduces hand fatigue and three included nozzle attachments, in the $100 to $200 tier. Its use is small: sweeping sawdust, clippings and dust from hard surfaces rather than moving leaves.

It ranks seventh because 100 CFM is the lowest in the group, half of the weakest Craftsman. It does fit the broad DEWALT 20V battery line, which many tool owners already have, and the nozzles let it reach tight places. For the same tier, the Craftsman 20V MAX kit gives twice the airflow.

Buy it for sweeping a deck or workshop. The caveat is plain: it will not move a yard of leaves.
products.skipIf: You need to clear lawn leaves.

products.name: Husqvarna 125B Gas Leaf Blower
products.verdict: A 470 CFM gas handheld with an ergonomic design. The only gas pick here.
products.description:
The Husqvarna 125B is a gas handheld that lists 470 CFM, an ergonomic design for extended use and a high-powered gas engine, in the $200 to $500 tier. Gas runs as long as you have fuel, so there is no battery limit for large jobs.

It ranks last in a Craftsman guide because it is a different kind of tool: gas, noisy and heavier than a V20. Against the V20 RP it moves 60 more CFM, but at a higher price and with fuel and upkeep. It is the only gas option here, so it serves as a reference point for what battery tools give up.

Buy it if you prefer gas for a mid-size lawn. The caveat is upkeep and noise: everyone else should stay with battery.
products.idealFor: Gas fans with a mid-size lawn.

whatMatters.detail: Craftsman V20 blowers range from 200 to 410 CFM. A 200 CFM tool suits patios and decks, while 380 to 410 handles lawns. Look for the CFM figure on the listing, and be careful when it is missing, as on the three-speed V20. Without an airflow number you cannot compare models, so ask the seller before buying.

Many listings sell a bare tool with a battery and charger sold separately. A kit costs more upfront but is usually cheaper than buying the pieces. The V20 RP and the 20V MAX include both, while the DEWALT 60V and the cheapest V20 do not. Read the contents list before ordering, and price the full kit.

A brushless motor is more efficient, giving better runtime and force from the same battery. It also wears slower because there are no brushes. The V20 RP lists one. Check the listing for the word brushless, and be cautious when a listing is silent. Others may use brushed motors, which cost less.

A dual-speed or three-speed selector lets you drop power near flower beds and boost it for wet leaves. A lock-on trigger saves your finger on long jobs. The axial kit has two stages, and the three-speed V20 adds a lock-on. Check the controls before buying, because a single speed is a limit near beds and gravel.

Figures like 50 percent less noise or 39 percent less weight than gas come from the brand. Use them as a direction, not a measurement, and compare CFM and weight where they are listed. Brand claims rarely state the test conditions, so treat a quiet claim as a comparison to gas and not to other battery blowers.

faq.q: Which Craftsman leaf blower is the strongest?
faq.a: The V20 RP lists 410 CFM, the top figure among Craftsman models here. The DEWALT DCBL772B is stronger at 600 CFM but is not a Craftsman and ships as a bare tool, so budget for a 60V battery.

faq.q: Do Craftsman blowers include a battery?
faq.a: Some do. The V20 RP and the 20V MAX kit include a battery and charger. Others, like the cheapest V20, may not, so check each listing and price the missing pieces.
For decks and patios, yes. For a lawn of leaves, choose 380 CFM or more. The 200 CFM models struggle with wet leaves and deep drifts, though they sweep a deck well.

If you own 60V batteries, yes: it lists 600 CFM. Otherwise the battery cost is high, and the V20 RP covers an ordinary yard with a battery included, so the DEWALT is rarely the better buy from scratch.

faq.q: Are the brand's noise claims reliable?
faq.a: They are manufacturer statements, such as 50 percent less noise than gas, and they come without test details. We have not verified them. Treat them as comparisons with gas and not with other battery blowers, and look at CFM instead.

faq.q: Should I buy a gas blower instead?
faq.a: Only if you dislike charging. The Husqvarna 125B lists 470 CFM but needs fuel and upkeep, and it is louder. A battery tool like the V20 RP is easier for most yards and starts with a trigger.

finalTake: Buy the Craftsman V20 RP for a typical suburban yard, since it is strong and ready to use. Step up to the DEWALT 60V only if you already own 60V batteries. Patio and deck owners can save with the 200 CFM V20 kits, and gas fans have the Husqvarna 125B as the single alternative.
